tasks.short: Prepare technical legal evidence and testify when needed

steps.what: Select and verify the actual workplace records and source evidence relevant to the proceeding
Arrange the selected evidence, identifiers and source references in the legal-document template
Write the factual technical account and its limitations from the verified evidence

loop.purpose: Draft a factual account from selected actual evidence
loop.input: Technician-selected evidence and explicit account direction
loop.output: Draft account with source references and uncertainty preserved
loop.check: Technician verifies chronology, attribution, omissions and every factual assertion; no invented causal or legal conclusion
loop.stop: One redraft then manual authoring; unresolved discrepancies remain explicit
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed document fields cannot phrase a varied technical account; native factual templates are used first

steps.what: Verify the completed technical evidence document against the original records and authenticate the final version
Save the authenticated evidence document in the same controlled document store
Testify in the legal proceeding when necessary and answer questions about the actual evidence and its limitations
outputs: technician's testimony and clarified evidence limitations

tasks.design: Test native evidence templates in {DOCS}, then use a bounded factual draft only for the varied technical account. The technician verifies and authenticates the complete document, saves it and personally testifies when needed; no court filing or external evidence send is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence layout and factual narrative composition take effort beyond source selection and testimony.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and source-grounded drafting can assist preparation without inventing evidence.
tasks.still_hard: An accurate quotation can still misrepresent context through omission.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what was actually observed and distinguish it from inference.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: controlled templates and source-grounded drafting can assist evidence preparation, requiring factual verification and human testimony.

assumptions: Boundary includes the statement's document preparation and testimony, modeled here for a case requiring testimony. External filing and disclosure remain outside this preparation route and are not performed by the tool.

Record owners supply actual dated records and source identifiers; authorized requester supplies scope. Technician verifies and selects evidence in s1. Missing or conflicting records remain explicit, not reconstructed by a model.

Native templates first. Shares are provisional scenarios; source review, authentication and testimony remain fully retained. Authentication is existing evidence correctness work after all content exists.
Same-store save is 1% fully retained. Gross 15 minus 1 upkeep leaves 14 net; evidence changes require renewed authentication.
unknowns: Actual evidence preparation effort and required authentication workflow
research_questions: Can templates and a bounded factual draft reduce preparation while preserving chronology, attribution and limitations?

already_counted.description: Review assembled evidence, factual draft and final authentication

incremental.description: Maintain evidence templates and review drafting failures

approvals.approved_version: authenticated final technical evidence document from s4; edits void authentication

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero for cases requiring manual narrative throughout; up to 9% if correction reduces central 14% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect actual hazard data for green equipment

steps.what: Read the actual new equipment or product information relevant to green practices and potential hazards
outputs: relevant source information and collection questions

steps.what: Collect potential-hazard data through actual equipment observations, authorized measurements and operator clarification
inputs: relevant source information and collection questions
actual equipment, workplace and operator accounts
outputs: actual hazard observations and measurement results

steps.what: Enter and check the collected hazard data with equipment identity, source, date and uncertainty
inputs: actual hazard observations and measurement results
relevant source information and collection questions

steps.what: Save the completed hazard-data entry in the same safety records system

tasks.design: Use native document bookmarks in {DOCS} to retrieve the relevant supplier information, then keep actual hazard collection and recording with the technician in {OPS_SYSTEM}. No model infers hazards from a product label or replaces site observation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant equipment information can take repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document references can shorten source retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier information may not describe the actual installation or exposure.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a hazard arising from the equipment's real workplace use.

ambition.what: No automated hazard certification or monitoring.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document references can assist source retrieval, while actual hazard data require observation and checked recording.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is safety records management. Boundary includes source reading, actual data collection, recording and save; risk acceptance or equipment release is not performed.

Supplier supplies actual product documents; technician collects and records equipment ID, location, observation or measured value, unit, date, method and uncertainty in s2-s3. Missing fields are manually resolved or marked unknown.
Native bookmarks and current recording forms first. Shares are provisional; only source navigation changes. Finishing and checking the actual entry stays within s3, with no new self-approval step.
Same-system save is 1% fully retained. Gross 2 minus 0.3 upkeep leaves 1.7 net.
unknowns: Current source navigation effort and availability of correct supplier versions
research_questions: Does native source navigation save time without confusing product claims with actual workplace evidence?

approvals.approved_version: completed checked hazard-data entry at end of s3; edits require renewed check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero where sources are already available; up to 1% with smaller retrieval gains than central 1.7% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep a factual daily activity logbook

steps.what: Recall and reconcile the day's actual areas visited and activities performed using existing job references
outputs: actual activity sequence and corrections to planned events

steps.what: Write and finish checking the daily logbook entry, including the actual areas visited and activities performed
inputs: actual activity sequence and corrections to planned events
outputs: completed checked daily activity log entry

steps.what: Save the completed daily log in the same logbook system
inputs: completed checked daily activity log entry

tasks.design: Configure native logbook date fields and reusable location choices in {OPS_SYSTEM}; the technician supplies the actual sequence using {CALENDAR} only as a reference. Keep authoring and checking together as ordinary log entry work, then save the finished version without adding a separate self-approval task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated date, area and activity headings add entry effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native logbook defaults and location lists can reduce repeated typing.
tasks.still_hard: A calendar appointment is not proof that an activity occurred.
tasks.human_edge: Record actual work and correct plans that did not happen.

ambition.what: No activity monitoring or expanded reporting introduced.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4; log access and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native logbook fields can reduce repeated typing while actual activity facts require the worker's account.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the daily activity logbook. Boundary covers actual activity reconstruction, entry, checking and save; no new formal approval or supervisor review is introduced.

Technician produces actual date, area visited, activity and relevant job reference in s1-s2. Calendar entries are prompts only; missing or conflicting facts are manually corrected, not inferred from planned events.
Native defaults first. Shares are unmeasured scenarios; 10% reduction of entry effort applies to repeated headings and choices only, not factual recall or correctness checking.
Gross 5.4 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 4.9 net. Same-system save has 1% fully retained; approval reference binds the finished entry at the end of ordinary authoring, with no added approval baseline.
unknowns: Actual repeated-field effort and current logbook defaults
research_questions: Can native defaults reduce typing while preserving corrections to planned activity and factual completeness?

already_counted.description: Author and check the actual daily entry

incremental.description: Maintain location choices and logbook defaults

approvals.approved_version: completed checked daily log at end of s2; later edits require renewed check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if defaults already exist; up to 3% for smaller typing gains than central 4.9% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Help direct rescue or firefighting during an emergency

steps.what: Help direct actual rescue or firefighting operations at the fire or explosion scene within the assigned emergency role
outputs: on-scene coordination and immediate response to changing conditions

steps.what: Exchange live operational information with responders and incident command by radio or phone

tasks.design: Keep emergency direction and live responder communication with the authorized people, using existing {TELEPHONY}. No new software or generated operational instruction is introduced into the response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conditions and information change during the emergency.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing live communications support the response without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Act within the assigned role while information remains incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize immediate changes and coordinate with incident command.

ambition.what: No automated emergency direction or extra response capacity.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: emergency direction depends on actual conditions and live coordination with responders.

assumptions: Boundary is actual rescue/firefighting assistance and live communication, not a post-incident report. No record write or independently authored dispatch send is established; live radio is not a hidden document transmission.
Inputs come from actual conditions and incident command; no new structured capture is required. Native reference tools cannot remove the real-time response step.
Shares are an illustrative split and all time stays retained. No software change means no incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Actual assigned response role and any separate formal dispatch-record action
research_questions: Review existing response workflow to separate actual record actions without delaying live operations.

incremental.description: No new software or recording process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On-scene direction and live responder communication are fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Technicians retain actual evidence gathering, testimony and emergency response; native records and bounded factual drafting assist documented work.
skills_to_grow: Separate actual activity from planned activity
role.ambitious_version: Accurate source-linked documentation without adding routine self-approval bureaucracy or shifting emergency authority.
